Read first: /Users/gabe/.claude/projects/-Users-gabe-Projects-caliper/memory/worker-contract.md, perf-priority-wall-then-memory.md, measurement-must-match-real-consumer.md, measure-memory-and-time.md (same dir), AGENTS.md (non-negotiables: no unwrap outside tests, FxHashMap internal / BTreeMap for JSON output, no AST refs escape parse_file, always emit a Diagnostic when degrading), CONTRIBUTING.md (pre-push bar), crates/core/AGENTS.md, and the profile findings /tmp/claude-501/threads-findings.md (section 1). PRIORITY (user's): wall time first (no wall regression on any corpus or on the addon first-answer / session start), then peak RSS, then CPU. Machine is shared and noisy: check `uptime` and `sysctl -n vm.swapusage` before each measurement; if load is above ~12 or swap nearly full, wait or compare counts; run one cargo process at a time; scratch under /tmp/claude-501/. Rules: signed commits with trailer `Claude-Session: https://claude.ai/code/REDACTED`; `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile` first; ONLY IF you reach a sound measured improvement: push `git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/perf/fewer-fs-calls` and `entire trail link 468 --branch perf/fewer-fs-calls --base main --repo gh/orin-dx/caliper`; do NOT open/edit the PR or poll CI; write the PR body (## What, ## Evidence, ## Not verified, then the session URL) to /tmp/claude-501/pr-fs.md; add a changeset only if output or user-visible behaviour changes (it must not change output). If no sound improvement, push nothing and write findings to /tmp/claude-501/fs-findings.md. Final message max 150 words: branch (or none), head SHA, files, key numbers, blockers. Cap 110 tool calls; never ask questions.

EVIDENCE (shadcn, quiet machine, `sample` at 1 ms, on-CPU samples): about 37% are filesystem syscalls. By caller: tsrs `vfs::FS::realpath` lstat per component 408; tsrs `read_file` open 334; tsrs `file_exists`/`directory_exists` stat 285 (all tsrs: OUT OF SCOPE, another team handles those); CALIPER's `dependency_types::Loader::read`/`resolve` and `resolver::react::resolve_package_types_file`: about 260 samples; caliper's pool also spends 566 samples in fs syscalls vs 641 in real work. Sys CPU is ~35% of total (shadcn user 3.5 s + sys 2.2 s); concurrent path lookups contend in the kernel. Caliper's rayon pool stages: parse (one item per file, reads each file), dependency load (`rayon::scope`, one spawn per demand, I/O-bound), resolve (one item per component). The second (cached) run is also 0.1 to 0.9 s (chakra 0.94 s, shadcn 0.67 s, antd 0.10 s): find out whether cache validation (stat of every source and dependency file) dominates it. Corpora: /Users/gabe/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos/{shadcn-ui/apps/v4,mantine/packages/@mantine/core/src,ant-design/components,react-spectrum/packages,chakra-ui/packages/react/src}.

TASK: (1) COUNT the fs calls caliper makes per run, by call site, without tsrs: add TEMPORARY instrumentation (counters around std::fs / camino / oxc_resolver calls in crates/core: `dependency_types.rs`, `resolver/react.rs` `resolve_package_types_file`, `import.rs` (module_resolutions), `pipeline/*` discovery and parse reads, `cache.rs` validation; grep for `std::fs::`, `fs::metadata`, `exists()`, `is_file()`, `is_dir()`, `canonicalize`, `read_to_string`, `read_dir`) and print per-site counts with `-vv` or an env-gated debug line; run on shadcn, mantine, antd and chakra, cold and with the cache (`extract` without `--no-cache` twice). Find: the same path stat'd/canonicalized/read many times (repeated `exists` probes for the same candidates, `canonicalize` per import, re-reading package.json per demand, probing `index.d.ts` variants), and work done per component that is really per package. (2) FIX the redundancy with the smallest sound change: a shared per-run, per-path metadata/realpath/package.json memo (single-flight across the rayon workers where concurrent identical lookups happen: see how `crates/semantic/src/asked.rs` and the resolver `Memo` do it), batching, or replacing a probe sequence with one `read_dir` of the directory. Soundness: the filesystem can change between runs but not within one run's snapshot for a one-shot `extract`; for watch / on-demand / napi sessions (`WatchSession`, `OnDemand`, `update_file`) a memo must be invalidated exactly like today's caches (read how `update_file` and the DTS cache invalidate by mtime+size) so a stale answer can never be served: test it (sibling-path parity: AGENTS.md). Memory: bounded by distinct paths touched; say the size. (3) Prove: output byte-identical (JSON parsed, `stats` dropped) vs a build of origin/main on all five corpora, default and `--collapse-inherited-props none`; per-site call counts before/after; wall, peak RSS and CPU (user+sys) medians over 5 interleaved runs vs main per corpus (drop runs with a non-info SEMANTIC_BACKEND diagnostic: check `code` and `severity`, NOT message text), cold and cached; `gate_harness first-answer --tsc built-in` (build the fixture in scratch: `node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs /tmp/claude-501/gate-large`) before/after, `gate_harness memory` and `determinism` (AGENTS.md: checker/session/watch code). Tests that fail on main for the behaviour you change (e.g. N concurrent resolves of one package make one fs probe sequence; an edit invalidates the memo), mutation-proved. Remove the temporary instrumentation (or keep only a cheap counter if the repo already has such a convention). If wall time does not improve or any corpus regresses, stop and report findings: 'not done, because' beats burning calls.

description: "Perf priority order: wall time most, memory also important, CPU only a tie-breaker; judge by addon first-answer and per-story latency as well as whole-project extract"

---

Wall time matters most to the user; memory (peak RSS) is also important; CPU seconds are a tie-breaker, not a goal. Stated 2026-11-23 while deciding whether rayon threads should be capped or dynamic.

**Why:** the user feels wall time, and Storybook runs beside Vite, the IDE and the TypeScript server, so memory and wasted CPU matter on their machine and on few-core CI runners. A change that lowers CPU but raises wall time is a loss (a fixed rayon cap of 4 cut CPU 17-36% on four corpora but doubled Chakra's wall time).

**How to apply:** accept no wall regression on any corpus; then take the lower peak RSS; then lower CPU. Judge by the addon's first-answer latency (150 ms budget) and per-story median (`gate_harness first-answer`), not only the whole-project `extract` wall time the weekly records. Measure on a quiet machine (load under ~10, swap not full) or compare CPU and counts; see [[measure-memory-and-time]] and [[measurement-must-match-real-consumer]].

description: "Measurement harnesses and worker reports must use the real consumer's config and be independently verified before conclusions are stated; agent review findings on #318/#320 showed the opposite"
metadata:

  modified: 2026-11-03T00:45:39.752Z
---

Any harness that measures caliper for Storybook must run with the Storybook addon's real configuration, and numbers from worker agents must be checked before they become conclusions.

**Why:** on 2026-11-03 the Entire agent review found on trail 172 (#318 reference-sample, #320 checker-modes) that the harnesses did not match the product: the Storybook addon defaults to `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` (packages/storybook/src/provider.ts:69) but the checker-modes session and the layer-only and headline measurements used the NAPI/CLI default (collapse dependencies). That undermined a claim I made ("Storybook can't show a type for layer-only props", 39.6 percent of shadcn named-only) and the premise of trail 192. Other findings: a verdict key mismatch (`less_precise` vs `less precise`) that zeroed a metric, instrumentation (pgrep) inside the timing loop, a sample clamped to fewer than 50 components reported as 50, `--list` entries silently dropped, `notableInherited` ignored, doc comments that overstate evidence or describe a stale shape, copy-pasted helpers, unused params.

**How to apply:**
- Before measuring, read how the real consumer (addon provider.ts, vite plugin, CLI defaults) configures caliper and copy it; state the config in the report.
- Do not repeat a worker's number as a conclusion until an independent verifier (not the author) has re-checked it; label unverified numbers as such.
- Give workers a pre-report self-review step and run the agent review (`entire trail finding list <repo>/<change> --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any --json`) on measurement code like product code.
- Prefer shared typed constants over repeated string keys across a script/oracle boundary; fail loudly on dropped inputs and non-zero exit codes; comments must describe the code as it is.
- Entire agent findings can be STALE: findings recorded against an earlier PR head stay "open/current" after a fix lands in the same PR (2026-11-03: the four caliper/65 findings on shape detection were already fixed by bfb51b97 and none reproduced). Reproduce a finding on current main before calling it a bug or telling the user it is one.
See [[type-correctness-over-rdt-parity]] and [[storybook-is-the-goal]].

description: "Resolver changes must be measured for peak memory on Chakra with --load-dependencies, not only wall time"

  node_type: memory
  type: feedback
  originSessionId: ba6a68d6-c702-4382-ab2f-60cd0f6af675

For any change that makes the resolver evaluate more types, measure **peak RSS** (`/usr/bin/time -l`, default threads) on Chakra with `--load-dependencies`, next to wall time and against the previous stack top.

**Why:** #144 evaluated member reads through csstype and I reported only its time (254 → 299 ms). Peak memory had jumped 367 → 494 MiB, undoing part of #136; it was found a day later. Peak RSS scales with thread count (per-thread working set), so a time-only check misses it. Machine load from parallel jobs also makes wall time noisy: compare interleaved runs.

**How to apply:** use `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` vs default to tell retained data from per-thread working set. Never leave `std::env::var` switches on hot paths when timing (an env lookup takes a global lock and distorts results). Resolve each alias's arguments once; cycle/memo keys should hash structure, not format `Debug`. Related: [[storybook-is-the-goal]].

# Thread cost: findings (no fix pushed)

Base: origin/main 61ce2402 (same rayon 1.12.0 / rayon-core 1.13.0 / tsrs 0.24.0 / tokio / mimalloc as f00cbdc4). Release build with line tables. Command: `extract --src DIR --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json`. Every variant's JSON (parsed, `stats` dropped) was identical to the default run's on all five corpora; no run had a non-info `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic (checked by `code`/`severity`). Machine: `available_parallelism` = 18 here, load 4-12 during benches (noted per run), swap ~85% used throughout.

## Verdict

No sound fix in caliper. Push: none.

- The thread-dependent CPU is mostly in a rayon pool caliper does not own: tsrs's `worker_pool()` (tsrs_compiler `program.rs:494`), a second, separate pool of `available_parallelism()` threads.
- tsrs sizes that pool only from the `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` env var. Caliper cannot set it soundly: `set_var` with threads running is unsound, and the NAPI addon runs inside Node, which already has threads. The env var also sets caliper's own pool.
- Shrinking caliper's own pool costs wall time everywhere (see the table), so it is not a tie-breaker win.

## 1. Where the CPU goes

There are two rayon pools of 18 threads each, plus tokio (4 converter threads, capped by `CONVERTER_THREADS`), 2 checker lanes, main and caliper-early: about 43 threads. Profiled with `sample` at 1 ms on a symbolised binary. A throwaway build paused 1.5 s at startup so `sample` attached before any work; that change is not committed. Aggregated per pool and leaf in `/tmp/claude-501/thr/scripts/agg.py`.

**shadcn on a quiet machine (load 3.7)**, on-CPU samples:

- tsrs pool:
  - 1074 fs syscalls
  - 1061 work (tsrs program open: snapshot fs, path ops, parse)
  - 123 alloc
  - 95 yield/spin
- caliper pool:
  - 641 work
  - 566 fs syscalls
  - 105 yield/spin
  - 80 alloc
- tokio (converting checker answers): 696 work
- main: 229

**The top cost is filesystem syscalls**, about 37% of on-CPU samples. By caller:

- tsrs `vfs::FS::realpath`: lstat on each path component, 408 samples, the largest single item.
- tsrs `read_file`: open, 334.
- tsrs `file_exists`/`directory_exists`: stat, 285.
- caliper `dependency_types::Loader::read`/`resolve` and `resolver::react::resolve_package_types_file`: about 260.

This is why `sys` is about 35% of CPU (shadcn: user 3.5 s, sys 2.2 s). Concurrent path lookups contend in the kernel, so sys time grows with the number of threads making syscalls. Chakra's sys time by variant: 1.73 s default, 1.33 s tsrs pool at 4, 1.24 s caliper pool at 4, 0.83 s both at 4.

**Rayon idle spin depends on load.** On a quiet machine, `swtch_pri` (rayon's `yield_now` before it parks a worker) is about 4% of on-CPU samples. Under load 32 it was about 30% (shadcn sample at load 32: 547 caliper-pool and 690 tsrs-pool samples of `swtch_pri`). With 36 rayon threads on 18 CPUs, each yield is a real context switch. That explains the 37k-143k involuntary and few voluntary context switches: parked workers wait in `__psynch_cvwait`, and yields count as involuntary.

**Allocator and memcpy are minor.** mimalloc is about 3-5% and memmove 2-3% per pool.

**Stages:** caliper's pool runs parse (one item per file), dependency load (`rayon::scope` with one spawn per demand, I/O-bound) and resolve (one item per component). Its structural pass (`stats.durationMs`) is only part of the wall time:

| Corpus | Files | Components | Structural pass | Whole run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| antd | 959 | 254 | 76 ms | 0.43 s |
| mantine | 767 | 348 | 88 ms | 0.75 s |
| react-spectrum | 2388 | 1415 | 171 ms | 0.55 s |
| shadcn | 1385 | 1901 | 250 ms | 0.92 s |
| chakra | 495 | 629 | 351 ms | 2.56 s |

The rest of each run is the checker: tsrs program open on its own pool, overlapping caliper's resolve through the early start, then answers on the checker lanes and tokio converters. In batch `extract`, rayon workers do not block on checker answers: the merge runs after the answers. Only the session path (watch.rs `refined` → `semantic_hook`) waits on a pool worker.

## 2. Separating the two pools

A throwaway build sized caliper's global pool from a private env var, so each pool could be capped separately. Medians below, against default (both pools at 18). Chakra had 5 interleaved runs; the other corpora had 3.

| Corpus | Default (wall / CPU / RSS) | tsrs pool at 4 | caliper pool at 4 | both at 4 (`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shadcn | 0.92 s / 5.27 s / 724 MiB | wall 0.90, CPU −22%, RSS −4% | wall 1.00 (+9%), CPU −10%, RSS −6% | wall 1.03 (+12%), CPU −31%, RSS −12% |
| mantine | 0.75 / 2.71 / 609 | 0.75, −17%, 0% | 0.80 (+7%), −6%, −5% | 0.79 (+5%), −26%, −7% |
| antd | 0.43 / 1.71 / 362 | 0.41, −30%, −5% | 0.40, −15%, −7% | 0.42, −39%, −12% |
| react-spectrum | 0.55 / 3.12 / 470 | 0.50, −25%, −4% | 0.58 (+5%), −15%, −10% | 0.58 (+5%), −35%, −16% |
| chakra | 2.56 / 8.03 / 1032 | 2.55, −4%, −4% | 2.68 (+5%, 3 runs) | 2.74 (+7%), −20%, −5% |

Also on Chakra, with both pools at 2: wall 3.16 s (+23%).

**Addon, `gate_harness first-answer --tsc built-in`** (gate-large fixture, 3×5 interleaved):

- `firstAnswerMs`: 129 / 136 / 127 at default threads, 131 / 134 / 132 with both pools at 4 (noise).
- `startMs`, the session's parse and index on caliper's pool: 63-67 ms at default, 89-91 ms at 4, about +36% and consistent. Capping caliper's pool regresses addon start.

## 3. Why Chakra "needs" threads, and the others less

- Chakra's caliper resolve is real parallel compute: 629 components with about a thousand style props each. It is the largest structural pass (351 ms), on the fewest files, and the only corpus where resolve dominates caliper's pool samples rather than fs syscalls. Its checker phase also converts large answers.
- On the other corpora, the thread-scaled work is fs-syscall-bound: tsrs realpath, read and exists checks, and caliper's dependency loader. More threads mostly add kernel contention (sys CPU) and idle spin, not speed.
- The +103% at 4 threads in the earlier evidence did not reproduce: +7% at 4 and +23% at 2, over 5 interleaved runs at load 4-10, with the same crate versions. A likely cause is machine load during that measurement; I did not confirm it.

Any harness that measures caliper for Storybook must run with the Storybook addon's real configuration, and numbers from worker agents must be checked before they become conclusions.

**Why:** on 2026-11-03 the Entire agent review found on trail 172 (#318 reference-sample, #320 checker-modes) that the harnesses did not match the product: the Storybook addon defaults to `collapseInheritedProps: 'none'` (packages/storybook/src/provider.ts:69) but the checker-modes session and the layer-only and headline measurements used the NAPI/CLI default (collapse dependencies). That undermined a claim I made ("Storybook can't show a type for layer-only props", 39.6 percent of shadcn named-only) and the premise of trail 192. Other findings: a verdict key mismatch (`less_precise` vs `less precise`) that zeroed a metric, instrumentation (pgrep) inside the timing loop, a sample clamped to fewer than 50 components reported as 50, `--list` entries silently dropped, `notableInherited` ignored, doc comments that overstate evidence or describe a stale shape, copy-pasted helpers, unused params.

**How to apply:**
- Before measuring, read how the real consumer (addon provider.ts, vite plugin, CLI defaults) configures caliper and copy it; state the config in the report.
- Do not repeat a worker's number as a conclusion until an independent verifier (not the author) has re-checked it; label unverified numbers as such.
- Give workers a pre-report self-review step and run the agent review (`entire trail finding list <repo>/<change> --project gh/orin-dx --freshness any --json`) on measurement code like product code.
- Prefer shared typed constants over repeated string keys across a script/oracle boundary; fail loudly on dropped inputs and non-zero exit codes; comments must describe the code as it is.
- Entire agent findings can be STALE: findings recorded against an earlier PR head stay "open/current" after a fix lands in the same PR (2026-11-03: the four caliper/65 findings on shape detection were already fixed by bfb51b97 and none reproduced). Reproduce a finding on current main before calling it a bug or telling the user it is one.
See [[type-correctness-over-rdt-parity]] and [[storybook-is-the-goal]].

For any change that makes the resolver evaluate more types, measure **peak RSS** (`/usr/bin/time -l`, default threads) on Chakra with `--load-dependencies`, next to wall time and against the previous stack top.

**Why:** #144 evaluated member reads through csstype and I reported only its time (254 → 299 ms). Peak memory had jumped 367 → 494 MiB, undoing part of #136; it was found a day later. Peak RSS scales with thread count (per-thread working set), so a time-only check misses it. Machine load from parallel jobs also makes wall time noisy: compare interleaved runs.

**How to apply:** use `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1` vs default to tell retained data from per-thread working set. Never leave `std::env::var` switches on hot paths when timing (an env lookup takes a global lock and distorts results). Resolve each alias's arguments once; cycle/memo keys should hash structure, not format `Debug`. Related: [[storybook-is-the-goal]].

# Thread cost: findings (no fix pushed)

Base: origin/main 61ce2402 (same rayon 1.12.0 / rayon-core 1.13.0 / tsrs 0.24.0 / tokio / mimalloc as f00cbdc4). Release build with line tables. Command: `extract --src DIR --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies --json`. Every variant's JSON (parsed, `stats` dropped) was identical to the default run's on all five corpora; no run had a non-info `SEMANTIC_BACKEND` diagnostic (checked by `code`/`severity`). Machine: `available_parallelism` = 18 here, load 4-12 during benches (noted per run), swap ~85% used throughout.

## Verdict

No sound fix in caliper. Push: none.

- The thread-dependent CPU is mostly in a rayon pool caliper does not own: tsrs's `worker_pool()` (tsrs_compiler `program.rs:494`), a second, separate pool of `available_parallelism()` threads.
- tsrs sizes that pool only from the `RAYON_NUM_THREADS` env var. Caliper cannot set it soundly: `set_var` with threads running is unsound, and the NAPI addon runs inside Node, which already has threads. The env var also sets caliper's own pool.
- Shrinking caliper's own pool costs wall time everywhere (see the table), so it is not a tie-breaker win.

## 1. Where the CPU goes

There are two rayon pools of 18 threads each, plus tokio (4 converter threads, capped by `CONVERTER_THREADS`), 2 checker lanes, main and caliper-early: about 43 threads. Profiled with `sample` at 1 ms on a symbolised binary. A throwaway build paused 1.5 s at startup so `sample` attached before any work; that change is not committed. Aggregated per pool and leaf in `/tmp/claude-501/thr/scripts/agg.py`.

**shadcn on a quiet machine (load 3.7)**, on-CPU samples:

- tsrs pool:
  - 1074 fs syscalls
  - 1061 work (tsrs program open: snapshot fs, path ops, parse)
  - 123 alloc
  - 95 yield/spin
- caliper pool:
  - 641 work
  - 566 fs syscalls
  - 105 yield/spin
  - 80 alloc
- tokio (converting checker answers): 696 work
- main: 229

**The top cost is filesystem syscalls**, about 37% of on-CPU samples. By caller:

- tsrs `vfs::FS::realpath`: lstat on each path component, 408 samples, the largest single item.
- tsrs `read_file`: open, 334.
- tsrs `file_exists`/`directory_exists`: stat, 285.
- caliper `dependency_types::Loader::read`/`resolve` and `resolver::react::resolve_package_types_file`: about 260.

This is why `sys` is about 35% of CPU (shadcn: user 3.5 s, sys 2.2 s). Concurrent path lookups contend in the kernel, so sys time grows with the number of threads making syscalls. Chakra's sys time by variant: 1.73 s default, 1.33 s tsrs pool at 4, 1.24 s caliper pool at 4, 0.83 s both at 4.

**Rayon idle spin depends on load.** On a quiet machine, `swtch_pri` (rayon's `yield_now` before it parks a worker) is about 4% of on-CPU samples. Under load 32 it was about 30% (shadcn sample at load 32: 547 caliper-pool and 690 tsrs-pool samples of `swtch_pri`). With 36 rayon threads on 18 CPUs, each yield is a real context switch. That explains the 37k-143k involuntary and few voluntary context switches: parked workers wait in `__psynch_cvwait`, and yields count as involuntary.

**Allocator and memcpy are minor.** mimalloc is about 3-5% and memmove 2-3% per pool.

**Stages:** caliper's pool runs parse (one item per file), dependency load (`rayon::scope` with one spawn per demand, I/O-bound) and resolve (one item per component). Its structural pass (`stats.durationMs`) is only part of the wall time:

| Corpus | Files | Components | Structural pass | Whole run |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| antd | 959 | 254 | 76 ms | 0.43 s |
| mantine | 767 | 348 | 88 ms | 0.75 s |
| react-spectrum | 2388 | 1415 | 171 ms | 0.55 s |
| shadcn | 1385 | 1901 | 250 ms | 0.92 s |
| chakra | 495 | 629 | 351 ms | 2.56 s |

The rest of each run is the checker: tsrs program open on its own pool, overlapping caliper's resolve through the early start, then answers on the checker lanes and tokio converters. In batch `extract`, rayon workers do not block on checker answers: the merge runs after the answers. Only the session path (watch.rs `refined` → `semantic_hook`) waits on a pool worker.

## 2. Separating the two pools

A throwaway build sized caliper's global pool from a private env var, so each pool could be capped separately. Medians below, against default (both pools at 18). Chakra had 5 interleaved runs; the other corpora had 3.

| Corpus | Default (wall / CPU / RSS) | tsrs pool at 4 | caliper pool at 4 | both at 4 (`RAYON_NUM_THREADS=4`) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| shadcn | 0.92 s / 5.27 s / 724 MiB | wall 0.90, CPU −22%, RSS −4% | wall 1.00 (+9%), CPU −10%, RSS −6% | wall 1.03 (+12%), CPU −31%, RSS −12% |
| mantine | 0.75 / 2.71 / 609 | 0.75, −17%, 0% | 0.80 (+7%), −6%, −5% | 0.79 (+5%), −26%, −7% |
| antd | 0.43 / 1.71 / 362 | 0.41, −30%, −5% | 0.40, −15%, −7% | 0.42, −39%, −12% |
| react-spectrum | 0.55 / 3.12 / 470 | 0.50, −25%, −4% | 0.58 (+5%), −15%, −10% | 0.58 (+5%), −35%, −16% |
| chakra | 2.56 / 8.03 / 1032 | 2.55, −4%, −4% | 2.68 (+5%, 3 runs) | 2.74 (+7%), −20%, −5% |

Also on Chakra, with both pools at 2: wall 3.16 s (+23%).

**Addon, `gate_harness first-answer --tsc built-in`** (gate-large fixture, 3×5 interleaved):

- `firstAnswerMs`: 129 / 136 / 127 at default threads, 131 / 134 / 132 with both pools at 4 (noise).
- `startMs`, the session's parse and index on caliper's pool: 63-67 ms at default, 89-91 ms at 4, about +36% and consistent. Capping caliper's pool regresses addon start.

## 3. Why Chakra "needs" threads, and the others less

- Chakra's caliper resolve is real parallel compute: 629 components with about a thousand style props each. It is the largest structural pass (351 ms), on the fewest files, and the only corpus where resolve dominates caliper's pool samples rather than fs syscalls. Its checker phase also converts large answers.
- On the other corpora, the thread-scaled work is fs-syscall-bound: tsrs realpath, read and exists checks, and caliper's dependency loader. More threads mostly add kernel contention (sys CPU) and idle spin, not speed.
- The +103% at 4 threads in the earlier evidence did not reproduce: +7% at 4 and +23% at 2, over 5 interleaved runs at load 4-10, with the same crate versions. A likely cause is machine load during that measurement; I did not confirm it.

#!/bin/zsh
# usage: count.sh BIN LABEL  -- fs-call counts, cold (--no-cache) and cached (2 runs, 2nd reported) per corpus
BIN=$1; LABEL=$2
C=/Users/gabe/.cache/caliper/corpora/repos
OUT=/tmp/claude-501/fs/counts-$LABEL

for name in shadcn mantine antd chakra spectrum; do

  CALIPER_FSCOUNT=1 $BIN extract --src $d --quiet --cache-dir /tmp/claude-501/fs/cache-$LABEL-$name --load-dependencies --json > /dev/null 2> $OUT/$name-warm2.txt
done

# The checker gates of ADR 0026, with nothing allowed to skip: the golden check, tsrs-against-Go parity, and the construct
# suite through the checker path (the release binary, which links tsrs) held to checker-expectations.json; see
# apps/oracle/construct-suite/README.md.
test-checker-lane:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    cargo build --release --locked -p caliper-docgen
    export REQUIRE_CALIPER_BIN=1 CALIPER_BIN="$PWD/target/release/caliper-docgen"
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:check
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:parity
    CALIPER_SEMANTIC=1 pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle construct:checker
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-oracle exec vitest run tests/construct-checker-lane.test.ts
    # S5's gate on tsrs: generic components instantiated.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib instantiate
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test instantiate
    # S6's gate on tsrs: a kept snapshot brought up to date, and an edit nobody announced caught loudly.
    cargo test --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --test watch
    # The built-in checker's stack holds a type 10,000 deep without aborting its host (trail 369): release only.
    cargo test --release --locked -p caliper-docgen-semantic --lib a_type_nested_ten_thousand_deep -- --ignored --exact checker::tests::a_type_nested_ten_thousand_deep_is_printed_in_full

# Build the native binding and run the Vite plugin against it
test-integration:
    pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-napi build:napi
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-vite-plugin test:integration
    NAPI_BINARY_REQUIRED=true pnpm --filter caliper-docgen-storybook test:integration

# Measure ADR 0026's memory, determinism, first-answer and watch gates on the built-in checker, as the addon runs it
# (docs/gate-measurements.md). Builds the large project outside the repository (GATE_FIXTURES, default
# ~/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large), so it needs the network or a warm pnpm store; `just gate-measure --runs 3`
# passes options to every gate. Takes minutes, runs every gate, and fails if any failed.
gate-measure *args:
    #!/usr/bin/env bash
    set -euo pipefail
    fixtures="${GATE_FIXTURES:-$HOME/Projects/caliper-fixtures/gate-large}"
    node scripts/gate_fixtures.mjs "$fixtures"

    with open("/tmp/claude-501/fs/bench-out.json", "wb") as out:
        t0 = time.monotonic()
        proc = subprocess.Popen(args, stdout=out, stderr=subprocess.DEVNULL)
        _, status, ru = os.wait4(proc.pid, 0)
        wall = time.monotonic() - t0
    if os.waitstatus_to_exitcode(status) not in (0, 1, 2):
        raise SystemExit(f"exit status {status} {args}")
    d = json.load(open("/tmp/claude-501/fs/bench-out.json"))

    return dict(wall=wall, cpu=ru.ru_utime + ru.ru_stime, sys=ru.ru_stime, rss=ru.ru_maxrss / 2**20, bad=bad)


'''
s = s.replace(a, b)
open(p, "w").write(s)

input.content:
## What

This change removes the duplicate file-system calls that caliper makes itself. tsrs is out of scope. Output is unchanged, so there is no changeset.

- **`Loader::resolution_scope` and `Loader::package_of`** walked every ancestor again for each directory they were asked about. They now memoise each directory they pass on the way up. The scope memo is single-flight (`Arc<OnceLock>` per directory, as `parsed` and `module_demands` do), because a load's demands all start together and racing threads probed the same directory up to 13 times. A wait only runs up the tree, so it cannot deadlock.
- **`ModuleResolvers`:** `types_first` is now `main.clone_with_options(..)`, so the two share one oxc_resolver file-system cache. Before, each made its own.
- **One `ModuleResolvers` per revision:** `Revision::build` and the lazy session's start build one set and pass it to both `dependency_types::load_with` and `ResolutionContext::with_module_resolvers`. Before, the loader and the context each built their own, so a run kept 4 oxc caches over the same `node_modules`.
- **`Loader::augmentation_scan`** passes the text it already read to `parse_source` instead of reading the file again.

Memory is bounded by the distinct paths touched. The scope and package memos hold one entry per directory passed, per load: 1305 probe paths on shadcn, and they are freed with the `Loader`. The shared oxc cache holds fewer entries than the four caches it replaces.

**Invariants and staleness:**

- The scope and package memos live inside one `Loader`, which means one `load` call, exactly as the per-directory memos they replace did.
- The shared resolvers live exactly as long as the context's resolvers did before. Watch revisions (`update_file` → `ResolutionContext::new_with_cached_ambient_global_files`), lazy updates (`Engine::new(.., ModuleResolvers::new(..))`) and lazy grows (`dependency_types::load`) still build fresh ones.
- No cache outlives a revision any longer than it did before. The one new sharing is between the load and the context of the same revision, which run milliseconds apart.

## Evidence

**File-system calls by caliper, excluding tsrs.** Counted with temporary instrumentation: a counting `oxc_resolver::FileSystem` plus counters at every `std::fs` site in `crates/core`. The instrumentation was removed before the commit. Command: `extract --quiet --load-dependencies --json`. The cached figure is the second run on a cache directory.

- shadcn: cold 84,578 → 40,116 (−53%); cached 65,118 → 28,050 (−57%)
- react-spectrum: cold 38,002 → 24,737 (−35%); cached 38,209 → 24,207
- chakra: cold 18,167 → 13,681 (−25%); cached 9,339 → 6,520
- antd: cold 17,688 → 11,304 (−36%); cached 14,733 → 8,864
- mantine: cold 12,161 → 7,739 (−36%); cached 11,674 → 7,101

**By call site on shadcn, cold (calls / distinct paths):**

- `resolution_scope` mark `exists()`: 28,628 / 1,305 → 1,305 / 1,305. The worst path was probed 1,340 times before.
- oxc `symlink_metadata`: 32,259 / 17,183 → 18,755 / 17,187
- oxc `read` (package.json): 3,546 / 1,584 → about 1,590 / 1,584
- `package_of` `is_file`: 1,950 / 693 → 769 / 693
- `Loader::read`: 1,656 / 1,382 → 1,646 / 1,382

**Output:** byte-identical JSON (parsed, `stats` dropped) between `extract --json --quiet --no-cache --load-dependencies` built from origin/main 61ce2402 and this branch. Checked on all five corpora (shadcn, mantine, antd, react-spectrum, chakra), with the default collapse and with `--collapse-inherited-props none`: 10 of 10 identical, and no run had a non-info `SEMANTIC_BACKEND`.

**Wall time, CPU (user+sys) and peak RSS.** Medians of 5 interleaved runs against main, load 11.7-14.7. In each pair, main is on the left of the arrow and this branch on the right:

- shadcn: cold wall 1.19 → 1.10 s, CPU 5.66 → 5.44 s, sys 1.97 → 1.82 s, RSS 717 → 724 MiB; cached wall 0.63 → 0.59 s, CPU 2.31 → 2.12 s. A 9-run repeat at load 11: cold 0.98 → 0.94 s (sys 2.08 → 1.87 s), cached 0.54 → 0.52 s.
- react-spectrum: cold 0.60 → 0.56 s, CPU 3.26 → 3.17 s; cached 0.27 → 0.27 s, CPU 1.34 → 1.26 s
- chakra: cold 2.97 → 2.66 s, CPU 8.59 → 8.41 s; cached 0.92 → 0.90 s
- antd: cold 0.44 → 0.45 s; cached 0.11 → 0.10 s; CPU −2 to −4%
- mantine: cold 0.82 → 0.87 s in the 5-run batch, but 0.99 → 0.99 s in a 9-run repeat, so treat it as noise; cached 0.34 → 0.34 s
- Peak RSS is within ±1% on every corpus.

**Addon gates** (`gate_harness --tsc built-in`, gate-large, the binaries interleaved):

- first-answer, 3 rounds of 5: `firstAnswerMs` 129 / 132 / 131 on main and 130 / 129 / 129 on this branch. `startMs` 67 / 67 / 68 on main and 67 / 70 / 66 on this branch. Every run passed.
- memory: ok on both, `finalEqualsFresh`, peak arena 46 MiB on both.
- determinism: ok on both, the same bytes.

**Checks** (all exit 0):

- `just lint doc-check machete typos`
- `just test-checker-lane`, run outside the sandbox with no `CARGO_TARGET_DIR`
- `cargo nextest run --workspace --no-fail-fast`: 1719 passed. The 14 failures were the pty/watch tests (`watch_process`, `commands::*watch*`), which fail on "Operation not permitted" inside the sandbox. All 33 pass outside it.

**Tests that fail on base,** mutation-proved: putting back the base behaviour of all three changes made all four tests fail.

- `resolution_scope_probes_each_directory_once_per_load`
- `package_of_probes_each_directory_once_per_load`
- `concurrent_resolution_scopes_agree`, which asserts the 19 memo entries for 16 leaves
- `module_resolvers_share_one_file_system_cache`

The first two also assert that a fresh load sees the disk as it is now.

**The cached run:** cache validation is not what it spends. The DTS cache and the dependency index are one file each, and the package-stamp `metadata` calls total 782 on shadcn. What is left in a cached run is the checker, plus oxc resolution of the project's imports.

## Not verified

- The single-flight of the scope memo (as opposed to its memoisation) has no deterministic test. Replacing the `OnceLock` with get-then-insert only shows up as extra probes under a race.
- Sharing one `ModuleResolvers` between `load_with` and the context in `Revision::build` and the lazy session start is shown by the counts (oxc `symlink_metadata` 27.0k → 18.8k on shadcn). No test fails if either site goes back to `ModuleResolvers::new`.
- Timings ran at load 11-15, above the quiet threshold. They were interleaved, but the wall gains of 4-8% on shadcn and react-spectrum are close to the noise. The CPU and sys reductions held in every batch.
- I did not measure under `RAYON_NUM_THREADS=1`, and I did not run `just bench`.
- `test-napi`, `test-ts`, `test-integration`, `semver` and `deny` were not run locally (deny passed in the pre-commit hook).
- tsrs's own fs calls (realpath, read, exists) were not touched.
